rv.q: It feels like a labour of love that, while faithful to the original, has a striking imaginative integrity in its own right.
As delicate as it is delightful, The Go-Between isn’t going to be to everyone’s tastes.
For all the determination to do Hartley proud, I found this a curiously austere night out.
I'm struggling to reconcile the ardent affection I felt for this show when it premiered in Leeds five years ago with the scepticism I'm seized by now.
'The Go-Between' is a perfectly tolerable night of entertainment, but there's absolutely nothing in it to set the pulse racing.
Mr. Crawford, as it happens, lends an entirely engaging, purposefully ghostly presence to a narrative that finds the aging Leo Colston shadowing his younger self...

cn.t: This delicate chamber musical adaptation divides critics: some praise its elegant, evocative restraint, while others find it too unobtrusive and lacking memorable songs to make a real impact.
